title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain
title_zh: 哺乳动物大脑的细胞尺度定律
abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational capacity, analogous to scaling up parameters in machine learning models. By contrast, the steering subsystem (hypothalamus, pallidum, and brainstem) scales via diversification of bespoke cell types to encode innate drives and reflexes, functioning as a high-dimensional biological "reward function." This framework explains the divergence in how evolution has influenced these subsystems and offers a unified lens for understanding brain architecture and the etiology of brain disease; furthermore, it may inform model designs for artificial intelligence.
abstract_zh: 最近的全脑细胞图谱揭示了一个一致的细胞结构特征：离散神经元细胞类型的最大多样性并不出现在神经元数量最多的区域（如皮层和小脑），而是出现在深部皮层下结构，如下丘脑和脑干。我们提出，这种差异反映了脊椎动物大脑中“学习子系统”和“引导子系统”之间的基本算法划分。学习子系统（皮层、纹状体和小脑）通过复制重复模块来扩展，从而最大化计算容量，类似于机器学习模型中参数的扩展。相反，引导子系统（下丘脑、苍白球和脑干）通过多样化专门的细胞类型来编码本能驱动和反射，充当高维生物学“奖励函数”。这一框架解释了进化如何影响这两个子系统的差异，并为理解大脑结构和脑病因学提供了统一视角；此外，它还可能为人工智能模型设计提供启示。
